historical_references.reference: Jigisha is a variant of the name Jaya, which was a common name for women in ancient India. Jaya means 'victorious' and was given to girls born into warrior or royal families to reflect their expected future success and power.

Another interpretation of the name Jigisha is that it may derive from the Sanskrit word 'jighasana' which means 'to desire'. This could suggest a connection to the goddess Saraswati, who represents knowledge and learning, as girls named Jigisha may have been encouraged to learn and pursue their desires in life.
